title: The Silver Line: A Memory-and-Succession Instrument
description: A memory-and-succession instrument in the docxology line set. It reads a declared succession picture — what is preserved, what is entrusted to whom, what is allowed to lapse — and returns a verdict about declared provision and review gaps, pinned to a registry digest. A KEPT verdict describes declared custody at a review date; it is never permission and never a promise that anything survives. Subtitle: What is preserved, what is entrusted to whom, what is allowed to lapse Code is MIT licensed; see LICENSE in the repository.

methods.name: Keepsake registry with retention, restraint and lapse families
methods.description: Declares kept items in a registry that carries restraint and lapse families alongside retention, so lapse is part of the declaration.
methods.evidence: the Silver registry carries restraint and lapse families alongside retention so the drift is refused in the declaration itself.

methods.name: Staged intake that sets aside malformed content with a note
methods.description: Normalizes each declared succession item at intake; malformed content is noted and set aside rather than crashing or being repaired.
methods.evidence: Intake first: each declared item is normalized, and malformed content is set aside with a note rather than crashing or being repaired into a fabricated value.

methods.name: Tag-intersection matching and present/missing evidence-label split
methods.description: Matches keepsakes to items by intersecting tags, then splits each keepsake's required evidence labels into present and missing.
methods.evidence: keepsakes whose tags intersect the item’s tags are matched, and each matched keepsake’s required evidence labels are split into present and missing.

methods.name: Verdict pinned to ISO review date and SHA-256 registry digest
methods.description: Each succession reading's verdict is tied to the review date and a SHA-256 digest of the keepsake registry that produced it.
methods.evidence: The verdict is pinned to the ISO review date and the SHA-256 digest of the keepsake registry that produced it.

methods.name: Worked example envelope: small lab-archive succession
methods.description: Runs the reading on a worked JSON example with one declared record, a named custodian and a partial evidence set, plus an empty-registry control.
methods.evidence: intakes a small lab-archive succession: one declared record with a named custodian and a partial evidence set.

key_findings: On the worked lab-archive example, the reading returns NEEDS_PROVISION, while the empty-registry control fails closed.
The formalism states that an empty scan set yields OUTSIDE_SCOPE with an intake note, and an unscorable registry yields NEEDS_REWORK with no findings.
A gap on a lapse-accepted keepsake is treated as a declared release (NEEDS_PROVISION), not a defect.
The paper limits verdicts to declaration coverage: it does not verify labels are real, judge quality, or guarantee survival.
key_findings_evidence: the reading returns the Definition 3 status NEEDS_PROVISION: gaps on lapse-accepted keepsakes are declared releases under Proposition 2, while the empty-registry control fails closed under Proposition 1.
An empty scan set yields 𝑂𝑈𝑇𝑆𝐼𝐷𝐸_𝑆𝐶𝑂𝑃𝐸with an intake note; a registry that cannot be scored yields 𝑁𝐸𝐸𝐷𝑆_𝑅𝐸𝑊𝑂𝑅𝐾with no findings.
A lapse-accepted keepsake with a gap reads NEEDS_PROVISION — a declared release, not a defect.

Every verdict describes declaration coverage only. The instrument does not verify that a declared label names something real, does not judge the quality of what is kept, and does not guarantee that anything survives its custodians.
